analysis.title: GS Basics: Retail Favorites. Vol Curve Un-Inverts. European Consumer (Rich Privorotsky, 12 Nov 2026)
key_insights: The rally on 11 Nov was narrow. Semis led (SOX +5.5%, ARM +12%, MU +12%) while MSFT, META and AMZN closed lower. Nvidia governance issues are forcing a rebalancing of capital, and NVDA fell roughly 9% overnight, weighing on the Asia tech tape.
The standout flow was Retail Favorites (GSXURFAV) at +495bps, its 3rd best day in three years. Three sub-$4 stocks accounted for 32% of US tape volume.
The vol complex has largely reset. The SPX vol curve un-inverted, dealer skew flattened and systematic L/S managers posted their best two-day return in nearly three years (+2.15%).

The desk sees lower risk, confusion around AI and persistent political and geopolitical concern. The open question is whether the bid is mechanical (low positioning, short covering) or the start of something more durable. Breadth is still narrow, but the market absorbed heavy Nvidia-specific pressure without broader capitulation.

Iran headlines conflict. There are reports of a contentious Netanyahu-Trump call over renewed strikes, which Netanyahu's office disputes, and suggestions that Vance is exploring direct talks, which Tehran has resisted. Iranian officials say Washington indicated roughly a 2w window before deciding on military action. A third US carrier group is heading to the region, possibly arriving mid month, though it may relieve an existing deployment. The desk has no conviction on direction.

Russia/Ukraine: Polymarket pricing for a ceasefire by December has fallen toward 10%, with March around 25%. Abu Dhabi talks produced agreement in principle on a prisoner exchange but little progress on territory and security. The desk sees progress as possible in 2027 and an imminent resolution as hard to argue for over the next two months.

On AI hardware and infrastructure, the desk separates compute demand from valuation multiples. Hyperscalers are best positioned given balance sheet capacity and contracted infrastructure. The four tactical overhangs are higher cost of capital, power and permitting delivery, the supply/demand balance entering 2028, and monetization velocity relative to capex. Near-term permitting concerns have eased, and the real worries are long-term supply absorption and ROI.
The desk expects the AI infrastructure trade to produce episodic, high beta trading rallies rather than pure buy and hold, with strong micro results coexisting with multiple compression.

On risk, it is unclear whether this is more than a bear market rally. A durable breakout probably requires lower rates, lower energy and broader leadership. Candidates outside AI infrastructure are hyperscalers, transportation, cyclicals and aerospace, and defense looks washed out. These groups struggle to work against an aggressive hiking cycle and high oil prices, so the desk expects chop rather than a breakout absent a fix in oil and rates. Reset positioning and elevated vol are short-term tailwinds.
The note lists a European Consumer piece, Euro Area 2027 Consumer Outlook - Winter Bills, Delayed Chills, by title only. No content is given.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning has been reset materially, volatility remains elevated and the market has absorbed an extraordinary amount of bad news. Low positioning and high vol are powerful short-term tailwinds, and the market absorbed heavy Nvidia pressure without broader capitulation.
tension_points.bear_case: This may be only a bear market rally driven by short covering. Breadth is narrow, and many groups struggle to work against an aggressive hiking cycle and stubbornly high oil prices.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A durable breakout needs lower rates, lower energy and broader leadership. Absent a fix in oil and rates, the desk expects chop rather than a breakout.
